title: Multi-SLO Escalator and Adaptive Thresholding for Canary Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Canary rollouts currently use fixed, single-metric thresholds which are brittle across traffic patterns and model families. This leads to unnecessary rollbacks for transient network blips and missed rollbacks when slow drift in token cost or throughput accumulates. Scope: implement a multi-signal escalation policy (an "escalator") that evaluates latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput together, and an adaptive thresholding subsystem that tunes per-cohort thresholds based on baseline distributions. The feature should integrate with existing rollout engine and provide observable decisions and manual override hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Escalator evaluates at least 4 signals (p50 latency, p95 latency, error rate, per-token cost, and throughput) and produces a risk score for a canary cohort
Adaptive thresholds are computed per-cohort using a rolling baseline window and can be configured with a decay and sensitivity parameter
Policy can be configured to take actions: WARN (notify), THROTTLE (reduce canary percent), PAUSE (stop progression), ROLLBACK (full revert), with clear audit events
Decision records emitted to events pipeline with all contributing signals and computed thresholds (for auditing and offline analysis)
End-to-end tests that simulate traffic shifts validate no false-positive rollbacks at <0.5% frequency under normal noise models
Docs and console UX: runbook, SLO tuning controls, and a timeline view of escalator decisions during a canary
design_decisions: Use a weighted z-score fusion for multi-signal scoring to make signals comparable across units
Maintain lightweight online baselines per-cohort with exponential decay (configurable half-life) instead of full-window storage to keep memory small
Expose per-signal weights and a global sensitivity parameter to PM/Owners for quick tuning
Keep rollback executors the same as current orchestration layer to preserve existing audit and safety guarantees
Emit both raw metrics and normalized z-scores in the decision record for offline explainability
implementation_plan: 1) Add Escalator service that subscribes to canary telemetry and computes per-cohort risk scores (backend) - owner: Jonah
2) Implement adaptive threshold library (C++ runtime & Python simulation harness) - owner: Marco
3) Integrate Escalator with rollout engine APIs to trigger actions (WARN/THROTTLE/PAUSE/ROLLBACK) - owner: Priya
4) Instrument decision events and wire into Events -> BigQuery for analysis - owner: SRE team
5) Console: small UX to show escalator decisions and tuning knobs behind an expert toggle - owner: Design
6) End-to-end tests in staging that replay recorded traffic traces and randomized noise injection - owner: QA
testing_plan: Unit tests for adaptive threshold math and z-score fusion
Simulation harness to evaluate sensitivity across open model families and sequence length distributions
Chaos scenarios in staging: network latency spikes, partial disk noise, temporary token cost spikes, throughput surges
Canary canary: rollout escalator to 10% of internal accounts, compare false positive/negative rates vs current fixed-thresholds
Manual runbook drills with on-call to validate manual override and rollback paths
telemetry_metrics: raw_signals: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, error_rate_pct, tokens_per_request, requests_per_sec
normalized_signals: z_p50, z_p95, z_error, z_tokens, z_throughput
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal only, Escalator in WARN mode, evaluate decision logs for 2 weeks
Beta: enable THROTTLE mode for staging canaries and 5% internal traffic for 1 week
Gradual: enable PAUSE/ROLLBACK automated actions for low-risk customers with a 2-minute manual cooldown
Full: enable for all hosted canaries with customer opt-in window and detailed release notes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-sensitive thresholds causing unnecessary rollbacks -> Mitigation: conservative default sensitivity and a staged enablement with internal-only experiments
Risk: Signal skew across regions/models -> Mitigation: compute per-cohort baselines and include region/model as cohort keys
Risk: Added decision latency -> Mitigation: keep Escalator CPU-light, compute on streaming aggregates rather than per-request
Risk: Customers lose trust due to opaque decisions -> Mitigation: log full decision records and show explainer in console; provide manual override with audit trail
